festivals: Raas Utsav / Raas Mela (Raas Purnima; the grand annual festival)

history.summary: Built between 1885 and 1889 by Maharaja Nripendra Narayan of Cooch Behar; the deity Madan Mohan, kul-devata of the Koch dynasty, was installed in 1890. The char-chala combined dalan (four-sloped roof) design blends traditional Bengali temple architecture with British-colonial influence from the princely-state era. The shrine also houses Kali, Tara and Bhavani. The Raas tradition is older than the temple: Maharaja Harendra Narayan began the Raas Mela in 1812 at Bhetaguri on Raas Purnima; after the temple was built, the fair moved to the Madan Mohan complex, where it remains one of North Bengal's largest annual events. The temple is now administered by the district administration.

name: Madan Mohan Temple
town_description: Cooch Behar is the former capital of the Koch princely state in northern West Bengal, centred on the Cooch Behar Rajbari palace and Bairagi Dighi; its royal-era temples, palaces and the Raas Mela make it the main heritage city of the region.

travel.airport: Bagdogra Airport near Siliguri (~150 km) is the nearest operating airport; Cooch Behar Airport has no commercial services
travel.railway: New Cooch Behar railway station (~5 km from town), on the main north-east rail corridor
travel.road: Central Bus Terminus near Cooch Behar Rajbari; North Bengal State Transport Corporation buses connect West Bengal, Assam and Bihar

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Raas Mela in November-December
